notes: Five steps and no evidence anywhere, which is the honest answer rather than a failure: this quest hands out no item and no key item at any point, so nothing about its progress is observable and every step's evidence is null on purpose. Bullet 2 is an explicit 'you must talk to all 3 of the following NPCs', with no order stated and all three standing within a grid square of Chumimi, so the three assistants share a group and draw at once -- a strict ladder would mark Biggorf and nothing else until the player happened to wander past the other two. Bullet 3 is the report back to Chumimi and is a genuine step; bullets 4 and 5 are the two possible OUTCOMES of that report (the corroborates-perfectly line with 500/250 Cruor and a seal chance, versus the seems-reasonable-enough line with 200 Cruor and no seal) and are not steps. The whole '== Fiend Descriptions ==' block, bullets 6 through 9, is an answer key for the dialogue menu -- three columns of flavour text per shape, colour and habitat, so the player can spot which two of the three assistants agree. Not one rung of it is something you do, and a verb scan would have made twelve steps out of it. The trailing 'Zoning is required in order to repeat this quest' is a repeat condition the addon cannot see and does not need. Fame 'aalt' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine fame regions, so it gates nothing and only the raw is kept. Tapoh Lihzeh straddles a boundary -- the page writes '(G-6)/(G-7)' and that is recorded rather than one half being picked. The '(A)' suffixes are wiki disambiguators; all four fold to plain in-game names, which the normaliser already handles.

report the two facts the assistants agreed on -- one symptom and one of shape, colour or habitat. Two of the three always agree and the third is the wrong answer; bullets 7 to 9 are the table for telling them apart. Answering wrong still completes the quest, for less Cruor and no seal, so nothing here is observable.

notes:
The main ladder is clean and unusually well evidenced -- six distinct key items over the nine steps before the turn-in, plus a seventh in the optional tail, each obtained at the step that carries it, so no item is evidence twice. Bullet 1's sub-bullet (you must zone following A Thirst for the Eons) is a precondition and stays a note. Bullet 2 is the only step that must HOLD anything: the Elder wooden box is appraised INTO Imprint device S, so the box is step 1's evidence and step 2's requirement, which is exactly the shape that gap wants.

The four Mnemonic Pools are one unordered group. The page lists them under a bare 'Mnemonic Pool locations:' line with no ordering language and closes with 'Once you've collected all four key items, return to Roskin', which is a collect-all and not a sequence; bullet 6's 'you can return the way you came to get the next one below' is route advice about a convenient order, not a requirement. Because each pool yields a DIFFERENT key item, every group member carries its own evidence -- unlike An Explorer's Footsteps, where seventeen identical Clay Tablets forced the evidence onto the last member alone.

'Mnemonic Pool' is the only name the page ever gives for what you interact with, and it gives it in a section heading rather than in any bullet. The page never says whether you click the pool or the cutscene fires on approach -- it only calls the result 'this cutscene'. Recorded as an examine on an object of that name: if no such entity exists in game those four steps simply keep their zone and grid and lose their markers, which is no worse than recording nothing. Those steps are the reason this quest is medium rather than high.

The turn-in is written as unnumbered prose after bullet 8, so its source_bullets is empty rather than falsely attributed to a bullet that does not say it.

The '== Optional ==' section is recorded as optional steps after the turn-in, the same shape Under Oath's epilogue takes. Bullet 9 warns the section is only optional if you never intend to start A Thirst Before Time, but the page is explicit that this quest completes when you return to Roskin with the four records, so relative to THIS ladder everything after it is post-completion. Bullet 12 is what Roskin asks for and folds into bullet 11's step. Bullet 14's pop-quiz answer key -- three screens of Adoulin trivia, Naakual names and the Twelve Orders -- is reference material for a dialogue menu and not a single step, and bullet 16's Speedy Score is an outcome. Bullet 15 does hand over a real key item, Heroes and Legends of Adoulin, so the quiz step carries it. Bullets 17 and 18 are both Roskin and are one step: 18 is a per-Conquest-Tally reward collection gated on a game day, which nothing in the packets reports.

Quest Reqs is a Seekers of Adoulin mission-chapter gate ('chapter four ... up to and including Balamor, the Deathborne Xol') with no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so it is flagged and gates nothing. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine fame regions, so region is null and only the raw is kept. The header's Start field carries no grid at all; (H-8) comes from bullet 1, and Palomel's square is never given anywhere on the page, so his steps carry a zone and no grid rather than an invented one.
